_readme: Caption looks: how the words on screen look and move. A look is a SETTING — switching it never re-edits the footage. Sizes are for a 1080-wide frame. `font` is a font id from looks/fonts.json (never a CSS stack). `zone` is where the line sits — a zone id from looks/placement.json (it moves off a face by itself when production marks one). `word_spacing` / `letter_spacing` are CSS lengths (`normal` = the font's own space, one space between words — no extra margin is ever added; an outlined look adds 0.1em so the outline does not eat the gap). `match-swipe` is not a row: it means build a one-off look from the teardown's caption read (font weight, case, colour, highlight, position). Only the owner signs a row approved.

looks.name: Bold highlight
looks.what: Big white capitals with a black outline, 2–4 words at a time, the word being spoken turns yellow and pops.
looks.when_to_use: Loud talking-head pieces where the swipe itself shouts its captions: big, readable with the sound off, the spoken word lit. No longer the default (V13, 2026-10-21: the look matches the app the piece pretends to be made in — `pick` below).

looks.name: Clean lower
looks.what: Sentence-case white words on a soft dark plate, low in the frame. Reads like a subtitle, not a shout.
looks.when_to_use: Calm, premium or clinical pieces; long sentences; an expert talking.

looks.name: One word
looks.what: One huge word at a time, dead centre. For hooks and fast cuts.
looks.when_to_use: Hooks and fast montage where each word is a hit.

looks.name: Word box
looks.what: Bold white capitals, 2–3 words at a time; the word being sung or said sits on a coloured box that moves word to word.
looks.when_to_use: Song ads and lyric-led pieces: the box rides the sung word (the owner, 2026-10-10, the first song ad — the swipe's box sat behind each sung word).

looks.name: Edits glow
looks.what: Instagram's Edits-app caption preset, rebuilt: a heavy, tightly spaced grotesque for the plain words, the words each phrase turns on (the step's action, the ingredient, the payoff, the comment word — the kit's caption_accent) in a tall condensed serif italic about 1.4x bigger, a soft white glow on every letter, each word fading in on its own as it is said into a line already laid out (nothing shifts), up to 5 words, aimed at the neck, under the chin and above what the person holds — never on the face or the mouth.
looks.when_to_use: Any organic piece that must look edited on the phone in Instagram (from the @mayalin_wellness swipe, studied frame by frame 2026-10-20). the owner: 'It can never look like it's being edited off of the phone.' Accent words come from the script's marked words (kit `caption_accent`).
looks.prefer_why: the owner 2026-10-20: captions on her neck, but 'you need awareness of the subject to ensure their mouths are never covered'. Aims at 38% (the neck in a chest-up shot), never lower than 56% (max_bottom_pct), and moves off any face or mouth the scene read finds, nearest first. V13 (captions) — supersedes the 10-12 'stack from the bottom' line for this look only (C1, 2026-10-21).

looks.name: Instagram / Facebook native
looks.what: Instagram and Facebook's own caption sticker: sentence case, white words on a soft dark rounded plate, 3–4 words at a time, low in the frame above the feed buttons.
looks.when_to_use: The default (the owner, 3 Oct: "these will mostly be on instagram and facebook so we need caption style that fits those platforms"; V13 2026-10-20: "It can never look like it's being edited off of the phone"). Moved here from looks/edit-looks.json on 2026-10-21 so both renderers read one registry (E6).

looks.name: TikTok native
looks.what: TikTok's own captions: white words with a black edge, no box, sentence case, 3 words at a time, low in the frame.
looks.when_to_use: A piece made to look shot and captioned inside TikTok (the timeline's style picker, 16 Oct). Moved here from looks/edit-looks.json on 2026-10-21 (E6).

looks.name: Reels bold
looks.what: Reels creator style: BOLD CAPITALS, white with a black edge, two words at a time.
looks.when_to_use: A Reels creator who captions in shouty capitals (16 Oct). Moved here from looks/edit-looks.json on 2026-10-21 (E6).

looks.name: Meta clean
looks.what: Meta feed, clean: white on a solid black box, a little larger, four words.
looks.when_to_use: A feed piece that should read as Meta's own clean subtitle (16 Oct). Moved here from looks/edit-looks.json on 2026-10-21 (E6).

pick._what: Which look a piece starts on, in this order: its FORMAT, else the APP it pretends to be made in (a substring of the kit's platform / app), else the default. Bottom (`caption-band`) is the default; a format with a look of its own keeps it (edits-glow aims at the neck). Never on a face or a mouth — placement.py moves a line off one, and audit.py checks the finished frames (V13, settled C1 2026-10-21). A run's own controls.json still wins.
